message.content:
Let  
\[
x=\frac{\cos\alpha}{\cos\beta},\qquad y=\frac{\sin\alpha}{\sin\beta}.
\]
Given \(x+y=-1\). Also let \(C=\cos^2\beta\), \(S=\sin^2\beta\), so \(C+S=1\).

Since \(\cos\alpha=x\cos\beta\) and \(\sin\alpha=y\sin\beta\),
\[
x^2C+y^2S=1=C+S.
\]
Thus
\[
(x^2-1)C+(y^2-1)S=0.
\]
Using \(x+y=-1\), we have \(x+1=-y\) and \(y+1=-x\), so this becomes
\[
y(1-x)C+x(1-y)S=0.
\]
Hence
\[
yC+xS=xy.
\]
The requested expression is
\[
\frac{\cos^3\beta}{\cos\alpha}+\frac{\sin^3\beta}{\sin\alpha}
=\frac{C}{x}+\frac{S}{y}
=\frac{yC+xS}{xy}
=\frac{xy}{xy}=1.
\]
So the only possible value is \(1\).

The answer is 1.
